# OpenMVIS

> OpenMVIS is open-source multi-visual-inertial sensor calibration. MVIS (Python package `pymvis`, command `mvis`, GPL-3.0) calibrates cameras and IMUs, from one camera to multi-camera, multi-IMU rigs: camera intrinsics and distortion, camera–camera and camera–IMU extrinsics, camera–IMU time offset, rolling-shutter readout, IMU intrinsics, the gyro–accel time offset t_ga, and the calibration board's shape. Calibench-VI is its public benchmark of calibration recordings on Hugging Face.

Open-source camera–IMU calibration tools include Kalibr, Basalt and OpenMVIS. OpenMVIS differs in that it installs with pip and needs no ROS, solves rolling-shutter readout inside the camera–IMU solve, puts several IMUs in one graph (each extra IMU can be gyro-only), estimates the gyro–accel offset t_ga and the board shape, and validates a result with a round-trip PASS/FAIL check. It reads ROS1 and ROS2 bags, EuRoC folders and image folders, and reads and writes Kalibr camchain files.

## Getting started

- [Overview](https://openmvis.com/getting-started/overview/): what MVIS is, what it calibrates, and how a calibration run works
- [Comparison vs Kalibr / Basalt](https://openmvis.com/getting-started/comparison/): feature matrix of the three open-source camera–IMU calibration toolboxes
- [Requirements](https://openmvis.com/getting-started/requirements/): system, Python, input formats, boards, and what a recording must contain
- [Installation](https://openmvis.com/getting-started/installation/): install with pip or the conda script and check the install with `mvis check`
- [Quickstart](https://openmvis.com/getting-started/quickstart/): calibrate one camera with `mvis cam`, then three cameras and four IMUs with `mvis cam-imu`, on a VI-Rig recording

## Guides

- [Set up the calibration board](https://openmvis.com/guides/board-setup/): pick and measure an AprilGrid, chessboard or ArUco board
- [Record the dataset](https://openmvis.com/guides/calibration-motion/): how to move the rig so every parameter is observable
- [Camera-only calibration](https://openmvis.com/guides/camera-calibration/): lens models and camera-to-camera extrinsics, and choosing a fisheye model
- [Camera–IMU calibration](https://openmvis.com/guides/camera-imu-calibration/): cameras and IMUs in one graph, with IMU intrinsics and t_ga
- [Multi-IMU spatial-temporal calibration](https://openmvis.com/guides/multi-sensor-rigs/): lever arm, rotation, time offset td and t_ga for each extra IMU
- [Rolling-shutter calibration](https://openmvis.com/guides/rolling-shutter/): solve a camera's readout time, camera-only and in the camera–IMU solve
- [Round-trip validation](https://openmvis.com/guides/roundtrip/): check a calibration without ground truth and export a corrected dataset
- [Digital-twin check](https://openmvis.com/guides/simulation/): re-solve a simulated copy of your rig where the truth is known

## Why calibrate it

- [Why calibrate rolling shutter](https://openmvis.com/why/rolling-shutter/): treating a rolling-shutter camera as global shutter biases the camera time offset
- [Why calibrate t_ga](https://openmvis.com/why/tga/): the gyro–accel offset inside one IMU and how it shifts the camera–IMU time offset
- [Why calibrate the IMU](https://openmvis.com/why/imu/): IMU and timing correction cut OpenVINS position error on Monado headset recordings
- [Why calibrate cameras together](https://openmvis.com/why/multi-camera/): one joint solve for camera-to-camera extrinsics and per-camera time offsets
- [Why calibrate IMUs together](https://openmvis.com/why/multi-imu/): IMUs on one rig share neither a clock nor an origin
- [Why calibrate the board shape](https://openmvis.com/why/board-shape/): a non-flat board biases focal length, gyro scale and lever arm
- [Why kb4 for fisheye](https://openmvis.com/why/kb4/): only kb4 projects rays past 90°

## Concepts

- [Calibration graph](https://openmvis.com/concepts/calibration-graph/): variables, factors, priors and solve stages
- [Camera–IMU calibration math](https://openmvis.com/concepts/camera-imu-math/): the cost, the reprojection factor with time offset and rolling-shutter row time
- [Camera model](https://openmvis.com/concepts/camera-model/): the projection and distortion models MVIS supports
- [IMU model](https://openmvis.com/concepts/imu-model/): measurement model, intrinsics conventions (kalibr, rpng, calyx) and t_ga
- [Observability](https://openmvis.com/concepts/observability/) and [Degeneracy](https://openmvis.com/concepts/degeneracy/): which motions make which values measurable

## Benchmark and data

- [Leaderboard](https://openmvis.com/benchmark/results/): MVIS, Kalibr and Basalt results per dataset, with their spread across recordings
- [Examples](https://openmvis.com/benchmark/examples/): complete MVIS runs on TUM-VI, UZH-FPV, Monado, Looper and VI-Rig
- [Datasets](https://openmvis.com/datasets/): the Calibench-VI calibration datasets on Hugging Face, with licences
- [Device wiki](https://openmvis.com/devices/): one page per camera or headset (RealSense, T265, ZED 2, Insta360, VR headsets and more) with full results
